title: Caught on cam: Punjab anti-drug activist shot dead after confronting chemist over 'drug sales'
content: Parwinder Singh Jhota was involved in a sting operation targeting a medical store in Mansa. He confronted the store owner about selling prohibited substances and had a heated exchange before being shot. Despite his attempts to escape, Jhota fell and was pronounced dead at the hospital. The police have identified the shooter, Ashwani Kumar, who fled after the incident.

title: IAF chief AP Singh takes final flight in Tejas, the fighter jet he once helped test
content: Air Chief Marshal AP Singh completed his final sortie on the Tejas aircraft during Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026. The exercise included multinational participation, highlighting operational capabilities and improving joint training. Singh has a long-standing association with the Tejas as a test pilot and has extensive flying experience. His tenure as IAF chief will end on October 31, after significant contributions to the Air Force.

title: 'Tears in both lungs': UP man's death under scanner; famous model accused of murder
content: Shiva Sharma tragically died after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartment on October 9. A post-mortem revealed severe internal injuries, leading to shock and haemorrhage. His mother has accused several individuals, including his girlfriend, of assault and murder. Police are currently investigating the circumstances of his death and examining CCTV footage and witness statements. Further searches are being conducted to locate individuals linked to this case.

title: USCIS warns immigrants: Update home address within 10 days or risk missing documents
content: US Citizenship and Immigration Services mandates that immigrants notify them of any address changes within 10 days. Failure to report changes may lead to missed immigration documents and important notices. Changing the address with the USPS alone is insufficient, as it does not update USCIS records automatically. USCIS encourages using their online system for immediate processing of address changes.

title: Gill pips Abhishek to win record 5th ICC award as Shafali completes India’s double
content: Shubman Gill has clinched his fifth ICC Player of the Month award thanks to a stellar ODI series against West Indies, which featured an impressive 110 runs and a record-setting double century that played a key role in India's success. Meanwhile, Shafali Verma celebrated her second monthly honor by being the top run-scorer in the Women's Asia Cup with an astounding total of 360 runs.

title: South Korea tests hypersonic missile: A new threat to North Korea's underground bunkers?
content: South Korea has successfully conducted a test of its domestically developed hypersonic boost-glide vehicle. This new missile system aims to enhance Seoul's ability to target North Korean sites as tensions rise. The hypersonic weapon can also potentially penetrate deeply buried targets, showcasing its destructive power. Similar developments are being pursued by other countries, including the United States and India.

title: CJP's Das, Ranka try to sneak into Jantar Mantar, detained by Delhi Police
content: Members of the Cockroach Janta Party gathered at Jantar Mantar carrying the national flag. They aimed to protest against the current government led by Narendramodi. Abhijeet Dipke reported on social media that certain individuals, including Ashutosh Ranka, were detained. The police intervened and took party members into custody during the protest. This situation highlights ongoing tensions between the party and government authorities over resistance movements.

title: South Korean employer paid him salary in dollars; tax department sends notice
content: A Karnataka man working in South Korea faced an income tax notice over his salary deposited in an NRE account in India. The Income Tax Assessing Officer claimed the salary was taxable in India due to his employment. However, the ITAT Bangalore found that the man had established his non-resident status.

title: Meet Iris Shen, 17, who tested blood cancer drugs and won $150,000 science prize
content: Iris Shen, a bright high school student hailing from The Woodlands, Texas, gained acclaim for her groundbreaking research on cancer. She explored a novel drug’s effects on clams to study its impact on blood cancer. The results of her experiment suggest new avenues for drug discovery, underlining the need for innovative approaches in medical research. This recognition underscores the crucial role of young scientists in furthering our scientific knowledge.

title: Moby bought Hollywood’s Wolf’s Lair for $3.925m, later sold it for $12.4m
content: In 2010, musician Moby bought Wolf’s Lair, a castle-like estate built in 1927 in the Hollywood Hills, for $3.925 million. He restored the 3.3-acre property while preserving its original character and period details. Four years later, he sold the estate for $12.4 million, approximately $8.475 million more than his original purchase price.

title: Zoho’s Sridhar Vembu tells staff no hike this year, tries to avoid layoffs
content: Sridhar Vembu, founder of Zoho, announced that employees will not receive annual salary hikes this year. This decision arises from increased costs associated with artificial intelligence and geopolitical challenges. Zoho has reduced its marketing budget and has not increased its headcount for 18 months. Vembu expressed gratitude for employees' understanding during this difficult period as he aims to avoid mass layoffs.

title: Antarctic sea ice hits third-lowest winter maximum in satellite record
content: On September 14, Antarctic sea ice reached its peak extent, covering around 17.59 million square kilometres. However, this year marks the third lowest maximum on record, indicating a concerning trend as it falls below the long-term average. The past four winters have each presented historically low sea ice levels, raising urgent questions about future climate impacts driven by this alarming decline in coverage.

title: Dad sold apartment, quit job; mom pledged gold: Making of India's latest WGM Sahithi
content: Sahithi Varshini Moogi’s journey to becoming India’s latest Woman Grandmaster is a story of many elements, with talent, sacrifice, and perseverance only part of it. Despite losing nearly three years to the pandemic and facing financial hardships and limited opportunities, she achieved the milestone with her father, Lokeswara Moogi Rao, as her coach. After selling property, pledging gold, and quitting his job, he continues pursuing her dream of chess greatness.

title: Naomi Osaka reveals how daughter Shai changed her life beyond tennis
content: Naomi Osaka has opened up about her mental health struggles, crediting motherhood and her daughter, Shai, with helping her find happiness beyond tennis. The four-time Grand Slam champion revealed how her perspective has changed since her 2021 French Open withdrawal, when she disclosed her battle with depression and anxiety. After defeating Maria Timofeeva at the China Open, Osaka reflected on personal growth, gratitude and learning to balance her professional career with life outside tennis.

title: Michael Dell-backed firm spent $375m upgrading Boca Raton resort; 40% condos sold
content: An impressive $875 million investment is set to transform The Boca Raton resort into a luxurious haven of residential condominiums. With around 40% of these high-end residences already reserved, pricing starts at $8.95 million and can exceed $20 million. This revitalization forms part of the resort's centennial celebrations scheduled for 2026, with construction commencing the same year and concluding by 2029.

title: New Yorkers queue for hours to buy old subway signs and seats at MTA sale
content: New Yorkers queued for hours at an annual MTA sale in south Brooklyn to buy discarded subway signs, seats and MetroCards. Station signs cost $500 to over $1,000, while orange subway seats sold for around $900. Filmmaker Spike Lee was among the shoppers, purchasing a Penn Station sign. The two-day event attracts around 4,000 visitors annually.

title: Pink ball in day Tests? Pollock’s bold idea to tackle bad light sparks debate
content: Shaun Pollock has raised an intriguing idea about the use of pink balls in daytime Test matches to combat delays from poor light conditions. His proposal came after weather interruptions plagued the first Test between South Africa and Australia in Durban. While cricket's governing body permits pink balls in daytime matches with both captains' approval, Ashwell Prince advocates for the traditional red ball due to varying team experiences.

title: Why Muslim-majority Azerbaijan is restricting hijabs in schools
content: Protests are sweeping across Azerbaijan as students and teachers react to newly imposed restrictions on wearing the hijab in schools. This controversy arose from changes in school uniform policies, igniting intense discussions about religious rights versus educational regulations. The government's stance underscores a commitment to secular education, yet many voices are calling for greater respect for individual religious beliefs within the academic sphere.

title: Drone attack sinks ship off Bulgaria coast, second strike in a week
content: A drone assault near the Black Sea coast of Bulgaria led to one ship's sinking and damage to another. The Maltese-flagged Chelsea 3 was impacted, but all crew members were rescued unharmed. Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev labeled the attacks intolerable and emphasized maritime security concerns. Similar incidents were recorded earlier in the month, highlighting rising threats to commercial shipping.

title: Bought Maruti Invicto, found repainted parts; commission orders Rs 3.6 lakh relief
content: In a significant ruling, a consumer commission in Kerala has mandated Popular Vehicles & Services Ltd to replace a Maruti Invicto car due to undisclosed repainted parts before delivery. Evidence indicated the vehicle had sustained damage, leading to unexpected repair costs. With the dealer unresponsive to the buyer's complaints, the commission deemed this a clear deficiency of service and directed compliance within 30 days.

title: Hyderabad techie dies after falling from 30th floor of his apartment
content: A 29-year-old software engineer from Suryapet district died by suicide at Golf Edge Apartments in Hyderabad. He had recently moved into a rented flat just two days before the incident occurred. A security guard found him on the ground and notified the residents of the apartment complex. He was later shifted to a private hospital, where he was declared dead.

title: Girl, 15, turns bullying ordeal into mental health initiative for others
content: Aanya Mukherjee's journey through high school was marred by bullying that took a toll on her mental health and self-esteem. After a disappointing response from her initial school, she transferred to a more supportive environment that fostered her healing. Passionate about mental health, she founded a nonprofit and advocates for the inclusion of youth perspectives in these vital discussions.

title: Indonesian conservationist, 14, plants thousands of mangroves to help communities
content: In Indonesia, young activist Harley Fatahillah Yodhaloka Sunoto is leading a passionate campaign for mangrove restoration and climate education. Through his Mangrove Warrior initiative, he has successfully planted thousands of seedlings in critical coastal regions, strengthening ecosystems and supporting local communities. By collaborating with mothers and organizations, Harley is educating on sustainable practices, with an ambitious goal of planting one million mangroves and launching educational programs nationwide.

title: Sydney’s Opal Tower declared defect-free nearly 8 years after cracks forced evacuation
content: After nearly eight years of uncertainty, Sydney's Opal Tower has officially been declared defect-free, following significant structural issues uncovered in December 2018. This crisis led to evacuations, extensive repairs, and legal conflicts regarding the building's safety standards. Most residents have safely returned after comprehensive rectification processes, and property owners will receive compensation along with a 20-year structural warranty.

title: Meet Harrison Nott, 16, whose bedroom towel business now makes £750,000 a year
content: Harrison Nott, a 16-year-old entrepreneur from Essex, England, started CoolTowel in his bedroom in 2023. After winning a global pitching competition and attracting investor Rio Ferdinand, his cooling towel business generated over £750,000 in revenue this year. Despite sales success, stock shortages, copycats and operating costs remain challenges as he pursues profitability full-time.

title: HCLTech jumps 7%, TCS up 5%: Why are IT stocks rallying
content: Dalal Street saw a surge as IT stocks soared following strong quarterly earnings from industry giants. HCLTech and Tata Consultancy Services were at the forefront, with their share prices climbing significantly. However, this rally comes amidst a tougher year for IT stocks, which have dipped by 23%. Investor concerns remain about inflation and fluctuating crude oil prices, with the global tech landscape also impacted by chip industry developments.

title: Ronaldo scores amid Riyadh security scare to close in on 1,000 career goals
content: Cristiano Ronaldo edged closer to the monumental milestone of 1,000 career goals by netting a goal for Al-Nassr in their AFC Champions League match. Although security alerts caused a postponement against Neftchi Fergana, which caused discomfort among fans and players, Al-Nassr clinched a 3-1 victory with Ronaldo being instrumental. A pending dispute with the Portuguese Football Federation, however, looms over him.

title: Gold price prediction: What is the outlook for the yellow metal today
content: Gold price prediction today: Gold prices are seeing ome fluctuations recently, influenced by geopolitical tensions and economic data. Recent attacks on Saudi Arabia have raised concerns about regional stability and oil prices. The US Dollar has strengthened, impacting gold prices and local currencies like the rupee. Expectations of future Fed rate hikes present additional challenges for gold.

title: Madras HC upholds TN Speaker's acceptance of resignations of 6 AIADMK MLAs
content: The Madras high court ruled that the resignations of six AIADMK MLAs were valid and voluntary. The speaker's acceptance of the resignations was deemed constitutionally appropriate under the Tenth Schedule. The court clarified that resignation and disqualification are separate constitutional processes within the governing framework. Additionally, it mandated the speaker to resolve pending disqualification proceedings within two months.

title: Sarah, first Zimbabwean female umpire in Women's T20 WC, passes away at 36
content: Former Zimbabwe cricketer and umpire Sarah Dambanevana has died in Harare at 36 after months in hospital following a medical procedure. She represented Zimbabwe from 2009 to 2014 before becoming an international umpire. In 2023, she became the first Zimbabwean woman to officiate a World Cup final and later worked at the 2024 and 2025 women's World Cups.

title: Tenant's Rs 10L deposit claim fails; Delhi HC orders payment for unauthorised stay
content: The case involved a tenant, who rented a 238.38 sq. ft shop in 2014 from a couple in Delhi. The agreed monthly rent was Rs 25,500. However, the 11-month rent agreement was never registered. The tenant subsequently claimed that he had paid the landlords Rs 10 lakh in cash as a security deposit between November 2016 and March 2017.

title: India's economic story in fast lane, IMF projects 7% GDP growth for FY27 and FY28
content: India is projected to maintain a robust growth rate of 7% in both 2026 and 2027, bolstered by strong domestic demand and a thriving services sector, according to the International Monetary Fund. Positive revisions from the World Bank and OECD highlight resilience amid consumption patterns. However, challenges such as rising energy prices and geopolitical tensions could impact this trajectory, yet India's economic growth remains strong compared to other major nations.

title: 6.7 magnitude earthquake hits central Mid-Atlantic Ridge
content:
Earthquake of magnitude 6.7 strikes Mid-Atlantic Ridge at 10 km depth (Reuters representative image)

A magnitude 6.7 earthquake struck the central Mid-Atlantic Ridge on Tuesday at 11:14 am IST, according to the United States Geological Survey (USGS). The earthquake took place at a depth of 10 km. Earlier in the day, an earthquake of magnitude 6.1 struck Panama at 4:50:37 am IST, according to the National Centre for Seismology (NCS). The tremor was recorded at a depth of 10 km, with its epicentre located at latitude 7.683 degrees north and longitude 81.405 degrees west. The earthquake came days after a powerful tremor struck the country and triggered a series of aftershocks.
